The Three-Layer Addressing System

Maps between three coordinate systems for efficient computation with user-friendly interfaces.

Why Three Layers?

Problem 1: External IDs are sparse

  • Bus numbers: 4001, 4502, 4211 (not 1, 2, 3)
  • Can't use as array indices (waste memory)
  • Need dense indices: 1, 2, 3...

Problem 2: Array access needs contiguous indices

  • Julia arrays use 1-based indexing
  • Cache-friendly memory needs sequential access
  • Solution: Internal indices (1, 2, 3...)

Problem 3: Solvers need flat vectors

  • All angles in positions 1-14
  • All voltages in positions 15-28
  • Or voltages first (for better Jacobian structure)
  • Solution: DAE addresses specify solver memory layout

Each layer solves exactly one problem.

Layer 1: External IDs → Internal Indices

Mapper: IndexOrder

Example:

  • Bus numbers [101, 205, 103] from file
  • Map to internal [1, 2, 3]
  • Lookup: order.indices[:Bus][101] → 1

When created: SystemModel construction (once)

Storage:

sys.order.indices[:Bus]       # Dict{Int,Int}: external → internal
sys.order.indices[:PQ]         # Same for each model type

Usage:

# Models store external IDs
pq.i = 101  # External bus number

# Look up internal index
internal_idx = sys.order.indices[:Bus][101]  # → 1

# Access bus voltage
vm = sys.models.Bus.vm[internal_idx]  # → sys.models.Bus.vm[1]

Handles: Sparse, non-contiguous external IDs → Dense, contiguous internal indices

Layer 2: Internal Indices → DAE Addresses

Mapper: AddressManager

Example (14-bus system with PowerInjection formulation):

  • 28 algebraic variables total (14 θ + 14 V)
  • Natural addressing: θ at 1-14, V at 15-28
  • Bus 1 (internal index 1): θ at address 1, V at address 15
  • Bus 2 (internal index 2): θ at address 2, V at address 16

When created: ACPowerFlowProblem construction (per-formulation)

Storage:

# Address vector for bus voltages
am.assignments[:Bus].by_type[AlgebVar()][:v]
# → [15, 16, 17, ..., 28]

# Element i = DAE address for bus i's voltage

Why formulation-specific:

  • PowerInjection: θ, V variables
  • CurrentInjection: Vr, Vi variables
  • Same system, different variable sets → different addresses

Addressing strategies:

  • NaturalAddressing - Group by type (all θ, then all V)
  • AMDAddressing - Minimize sparse matrix fill-in
  • CustomPermutation - User-provided ordering

Layer 3: Foreign References (Precomputed Shortcut)

Problem: Models reference other models repeatedly

Example:

  • PV generator at bus 4001
  • Needs bus voltage thousands of times (during Newton iterations)
  • Full path: External 4001 → Internal 15 → Addresses

Solution: Precompute external → internal hop

Storage:

foreign_refs[:PV][:i]  # Vector of internal Bus indices
# foreign_refs[:PV][:i][1] = 15 means "PV gen 1 at bus 15"

Created: SystemModel construction (examines metadata reference fields)

Benefit: Eliminates dictionary lookups in hot paths

Helper Functions

# Get internal indices for PV generator buses
bus_indices = get_ext_indices(sol, :PV, :i)

# Get from-bus indices for branches
from_bus = get_ext_indices(sol, :Branch, :i)
to_bus = get_ext_indices(sol, :Branch, :j)

# Get field values from referenced model (combines lookup + field access)
basekv = get_ext_field(sol, :PV, :i, :basekv)  # Base voltages for PV buses

API Boundaries

Layer 1 API (IndexOrder)

Input: Model collections with external IDs in struct fields

Output: order.indices[model_type][external_id] → internal_index

Used by: System for array access, users for specifying devices

Layer 2 API (AddressManager)

Input: SystemModel + formulation trait

Output: am.assignments[model][addr_type][var_name] → Vector{Int}

  • Element i = DAE address for instance i's variable

Used by: Gather/scatter operations during residual evaluation

Layer 3 API (Foreign References)

Input: Model metadata (Terminal/reference field declarations)

Output: foreign_refs[model][field] → Vector{Int}

  • Internal indices for referenced model instances

Used by: Models during residual evaluation (fast lookups)

Concrete Example: Variable Access

User request: get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, (4001,))

Step 1: External → Internal

external_id = 4001
internal_idx = sol.prob.sys.order.indices[:Bus][4001]  # → 15

Step 2: Internal → DAE Address

v_addresses = sol.prob.address_manager.assignments[:Bus].by_type[AlgebVar()][:v]
dae_addr = v_addresses[15]  # → 58

Step 3: Read from DAE Vector

value = sol.dae.y[58]  # → 1.05 (per-unit)

Step 4 (optional): Convert to Physical Units

coeff = sol.prob.sys.pu_coeffs.Bus.vm[15]  # → 138.0 kV base
physical = value * coeff  # → 144.9 kV

Changing Address Layout

Flexibility: Only touch AddressManager, external API unchanged

Example strategies:

  • Natural: All θ, then all V (intuitive)
  • AMD: Minimize sparse fill-in (performance)
  • Bus-grouped: θ,V for bus 1, then θ,V for bus 2 (locality)

Implementation:

# Try different addressing strategy
prob1 = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection(), NaturalAddressing())
prob2 = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection(), AMDAddressing())

# Same system, same external IDs
# Different DAE address layouts
# No model code changes

Why it works:

  • External ID mapping unchanged (bus 4001 still internal 15)
  • Models don't see DAE addresses directly
  • ResidualBuffers handle gather/scatter automatically

This is why AddressManager lives in problem, not SystemModel.

Extension Points

Custom Addressing Strategies

Create AddressingStrategy subtype:

struct MyAddressing <: AddressingStrategy end

function assign_addresses!(am, sys, formulation, ::MyAddressing)
    # Your assignment algorithm
    # Assign unique addresses to each variable
end

Pass to problem: ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, formulation, MyAddressing())

New Models with Cross-References

Declare references in metadata:

const MY_MODEL_TERMINALS = (Terminal(:Bus, :i),)

const MY_MODEL_EXT_PARAMS = [
    ExtParam(:basekv, MY_MODEL_TERMINALS[1], :basekv, ...)
]

System automatically creates foreign_refs[:MyModel][:i] during construction.

Alternative Index Mapping

Current ext2int: Contiguous 1-based in file order

Alternatives:

  • Sort by bus number
  • Group by zone/area
  • Custom ordering

Requirement: Output must be IndexOrder with correct dictionary structure.

Multi-Level Hierarchies

Add new mapping structures for zone/area aggregations. Compose with existing three layers. Core system unmodified.

Key Principle

Maintain clear separation:

  • External IDs - User-facing, stable across solutions
  • Internal indices - Implementation-efficient array positions
  • DAE addresses - Solver-specific equation vector positions

Each layer has one job, provides stable interface to layer above.
